title: Customer Adoption Segmentation and Action Playbook
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a repeatable approach to segmenting enterprise tenants after go-live and driving measurable adoption actions. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Technical Account Managers (TAMs), Customer Support Engineers (CSEs), and partner Solutions Engineers. The goal is to create prioritized, automated, and measurable interventions that improve stability, product value realization, and renewal velocity.

Scope:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private tenants in early to mid-post-go-live (day 7 -> month 6).
- Excludes pilot/proof-of-concept tenants still under active engineering feature trials.
- Intended to complement the first-90-days operational checklist; this document focuses on segmentation, signals, and playbook actions.

Key definitions:
- Tenant: customer-owned instance registered in Redwood control plane.
- Active Call: successful API request to generation/embedding endpoints in the last 30 days.
- Primary SLA: the latency and availability commitment for a tenant (e.g., 95th pct latency < 350ms, availability 99.9%).
- Adoption Index: composite score (0-100) combining usage, success rate, cost efficiency, and eval pass rate.

Segmentation framework (high level):
1) Business priority (tier)
   - Strategic: enterprise logo accounts with reserved capacity or contract value > $300k/year.
   - Growth: customers with sustained usage committing to expand in 90 days.
   - Self-serve: small tenants using hosted API only.
2) Technical posture
   - Green: stable requests, low error rate, KV-cache hit rate > 60%.
   - Yellow: intermittent errors, increased latency, or model quality regressions detected.
   - Red: sustained errors, rollout failures, or repeated customer escalations.
3) Adoption maturity (using Adoption Index)
   - Explorer (0-29): low integration, few API calls, limited telemetry.
   - Integrator (30-69): integrations live, moderate traffic, early caching/batching patterns.
   - Optimizer (70-100): mature telemetry, cost controls, good latency and quality metrics.

Operational signals and thresholds (examples):
- Traffic signal: < 50 unique user sessions or < 1k API calls / week -> exploration alert.
- Stability signal: 5xx rate > 1% for 30m or 0.5% sustained for 24h -> stability alert.
- Latency signal: P95 generation latency > 750ms for 15m -> investigate kernel/runtime or route fallback.
- Quality signal: Regression eval failure on core prompt set (accuracy drop >= 5%) -> model quality alert.
- Cost signal: Cost per 1k tokens exceeds baseline by 40% for billing period -> cost anomaly.

Adoption actions by segment (playbook table):
- Explorer -> Step actions:
  1) Automated email + usage tips (day 7) including quickstart snippets for prefix caching and batching.
  2) Invite to a 30-minute onboarding clinic (TAM) if calls remain low at day 14.
  3) Provide pre-configured prompt set and eval harness for basic quality checks.
- Integrator -> Step actions:
  1) Schedule 60-minute technical review within 7 business days of reaching Integrator threshold.
  2) Provide recommended batching/quantization profiles and cost-saving suggestions via Redwood Optimize.
  3) Configure synthetic journey monitors and run weekly synthetic QBR checks.
- Optimizer -> Step actions:
  1) Quarterly QBR focusing on model economics and feature/add-on expansion.
  2) Offer joint runbook and SLO tuning session with Eng-SRE.
  3) Propose Dedicated reservation sizing review for cost savings.

Example SLA mapping matrix (table):
| Tenant Tier | Minimum monitoring | SLOs tracked | Standard intervention | Escalation owner |
|-------------|---------------------|--------------|----------------------|------------------|
| Strategic   | 1m metrics; traces   | Availability 99.9%; P95 < 350ms | TAM-led weekly sync | Escalation: Eng-SRE on-call |
| Growth      | 5m metrics; traces   | Availability 99.5%; P95 < 500ms | CSM technical review | CSE + TAM |
| Self-serve  | 1h metrics           | Availability 99.0%; P95 < 800ms | Auto-notifications + docs | Support Tier 1 |

Runbook: Stability incident (example trigger: 5xx spike > 1% sustained 30m)
1) Triage (0-15m):
   - On-call CSE checks tenant dashboard: error rates, recent deploys, model variants in use.
   - Run quick query: SELECT count(*) as errors, time_bucket('1m', ts) FROM tenant_logs WHERE tenant_id = '<TENANT>' AND status >= 500 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 60;
   - If spike aligns with deploy, tag incident as "deploy-regression" and notify Eng-Serving-Runtime.
2) Mitigation (15-45m):
   - If model fallback configured, execute route-switch to warm-compatible-variant: POST /admin/tenants/<TENANT>/route-fallback {"variant":"stable-v1"} (use admin API).
   - If KV cache invalidation suspected, issue cache-warm: POST /admin/tenants/<TENANT>/kvcache/warm?prefix=default
3) Customer comms (15-60m):
   - CSM/TAM sends templated status update to customer with RCA-in-progress tag and ETA for next update.
4) Remediation (60m+):
   - Coordinate rollback or patch with eng. Produce post-incident checklist and RCA in the ticket.
   - If SLA credit condition met, notify Finance SLA team per contract matrix.

Synthetic telemetry and QBR metrics (recommended):
- Weekly: Adoption Index, Active Calls, KV-cache hit rate, P95 latency, Error rate (5xx), Cost per 1k tokens.
- Monthly: Evals pass rate on canonical prompt set, model variance usage, reserved capacity utilization.
- Queries (example):
  - Prometheus P95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant_id="<TENANT>",route="generate"}[5m])) by (le))
  - SQL cost anomaly: SELECT tenant_id, sum(billing_tokens) / NULLIF(sum(successful_requests),0) as tokens_per_call FROM billing_usage WHERE month = '2026-01' GROUP BY tenant_id HAVING tokens_per_call > 1.4 * (SELECT avg(tokens_per_call) FROM ... ) ;

Customer engagement templates (concise):
- Low-usage nudge (automated): Subject: "Quick wins with Redwood: caching & batching tips" Body: short tips + link to one-click sample repo.
- Quality regression alert (CSM template): includes ETA, impact, temporary mitigations (model fallback) and link to eval results.

Escalation ladder (when to involve who):
1) CSM/TAM -> handles adoption nudges and scheduling.
2) CSE (Tier 2) -> owns tenant-level technical triage and routing fixes.
3) Eng-Serving-Runtime on-call -> required for regressions linked to model runtime or kernel failures.
4) Eng-SRE -> required for infra-level outages, capacity exhaustion, or long-running performance regressions.
5) Legal/Support-Contract -> engaged if SLA credit calculation or contract breach is likely.

Playbook automation recipes (examples):
- Auto-classify tenants weekly using Adoption Index with a scheduled job: POST /internal/jobs/classify-tenants {"window_days":30} -> outputs CSV to S3 and triggers CSM notifications for Explorers.
- Create synthetic tests per tenant and failover rules via terraform templates; sample variable file excerpt: 

terraform vars:
```
tenant_id = "<TENANT>"
synthetic_check_cron = "0 6 * * MON"
failover_variant = "stable-v1"
```

Operational checklist for first 30 days (concise):
- Day 1: Verify control-plane registration, API keys, and firewall peering.
- Day 3: Confirm telemetry ingestion and synthetic journey baseline.
- Day 7: Validate prefix/KV cache configuration and run initial evals.
- Day 14: Reach out with technical review if Integrator thresholds not met.
- Day 30: CSM conducts adoption health review and proposes next quarter roadmap.

QBR agenda template (30–45 minutes):
1) Executive summary (5m): Adoption Index trend and business impact highlights.
2) Stability & SLO review (10m): Availability, latency, recent incidents, and mitigations.
3) Quality & Evals (8m): Results from canonical prompt sets and any model swaps.
4) Cost & Efficiency (7m): Token economics, batching/quantization savings, reserved capacity recommendations.
5) Roadmap & Actions (5–10m): Proposed improvements, feature requests, and ownership.

Ownership and SLAs for the playbook: 
- Playbook owner: Customer Success Operations (owner: Jordan Kim).
- Monitoring & alerts: Eng-Platform (onboarded to all tenant dashboards).
- Escalation owners: CSE (Tier 2), Eng-Serving-Runtime (runtime regressions).
- Review cadence: Quarterly review of thresholds and Adoption Index formula.

Appendix: Useful links and snippets
- Admin API examples: https://internal-api.redwood.ai/docs/admin
- Adoption Index calculation (pseudo): AdoptionIndex = 0.4*normalized_usage + 0.25*stability_score + 0.2*efficiency_score + 0.15*eval_pass_rate
- Contact list: TAM rotation roster (internal link), Eng-SRE on-call (pager link), Support Slack channel #support-tenant-triage.

Change log:
- 2026-01-15: Created initial playbook (Jordan Kim).
- 2026-02-20: Added SLA mapping matrix and runbook templates; updated signal thresholds (reviewers: Priya Menon, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Alvarez).
